content: 1. Fibrinolytic drugs are not intended for routine maintenance or reopening of central venous lines. 2. The coadministration of defibrotide with antithrombotic or fibrinolytic drugs is contraindicated due to pharmacodynamic synergism, which increases the effects of these drugs. 3. Defibrotide enhances the effects of dalteparin, desirudin, edoxaban, enoxaparin, heparin, fondaparinux, rivaroxaban, and warfarin through pharmacodynamic synergism, making their coadministration contraindicated. 4. Defibrotide increases the effects of diclofenac, diflunisal, etodolac, fenoprofen, ibuprofen, ibuprofen IV, indomethacin, ketoprofen, ketorolac, ketorolac intranasal, meclofenamate, mefenamic acid, meloxicam, nabumetone, naproxen, oxaprozin, piroxicam, salsalate, sulindac, and tolmetin via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Defibrotide may enhance the effects of platelet inhibitors, including escitalopram, fluoxetine, flurbiprofen, fluvoxamine, paroxetine, prasugrel, sertraline, ticagrelor, ticlopidine, and tirofiban. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Fish oil triglycerides increase the level or effect of defibrotide through anticoagulation. Monitor bleeding time periodically in patients receiving fish oil triglycerides and concomitant antiplatelet agents or anticoagulants. 7. Ibrutinib increases the level or effect of defibrotide through anticoagulation and may increase the risk of hemorrhage in patients receiving antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapies. Monitor for signs of bleeding. 8. Tranexamic acid injection and oral formulations decrease the effects of defibrotide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 9. Defibrotide increases the activity of fibrinolytic enzymes in vitro and may increase the risk of bleeding in patients with veno-occlusive disease (VOD). Monitor for bleeding. 10. Do not initiate defibrotide in patients with active bleeding. If bleeding occurs, discontinue the drug and treat the underlying cause. 11. Defibrotide is contraindicated with systemic anticoagulants or fibrinolytic agents, except for routine maintenance or reopening of central venous lines. 12. Hypotension (37%), diarrhea (24%), vomiting (18%), nausea (16%), epistaxis (14%), pulmonary alveolar hemorrhage (7-9%), gastrointestinal hemorrhage (3-9%), sepsis (5-7%), graft-versus-host disease (4-6%), lung infiltration (3-6%), pneumonia (3-5%), pulmonary hemorrhage (2-4%), infection (2-3%), intracranial hemorrhage (2-3%), hyperuricemia (2%), cerebral hemorrhage (2%), and hypersensitivity reactions (<2%) have been reported. 13. Hypersensitivity reactions, including rash, urticaria, and angioedema, have been reported. 14. There are no available data on the use of defibrotide in pregnant women. Advise pregnant women of the potential risk of miscarriage based on animal data. 15. It is unknown if defibrotide is distributed in human breast milk. Due to the potential for serious adverse reactions, including bleeding in a breastfed infant, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment. 16. Consider the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding along with the mother’s clinical need for the drug and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed infant from the drug or the underlying maternal condition. 17. Store unopened vials at 20-25°C (68-77°F), with excursions permitted between 15-30°C (59-86°F). Vials contain no antimicrobial preservatives and are intended for single-patient use only. Discard partially used vials. 18. Use the diluted solution within 4 hours if stored at room temperature or within 24 hours if refrigerated. Up to 4 doses may be prepared at one time if refrigerated. 19. Do not coadminister defibrotide with other IV drugs concurrently within the same IV line. 20.
